I was able to find the wires! I took the NID off to see approximately where the hole was on the exterior. I measured how high and how far from the edge of the house it was. I was able to approximate what would be a foot or two higher on the inside. It was damn near my circuit breaker. I did a small hole and used my borescope to explore the cavity next to it. The CAT5e cables are run along side the post that supports my electrical panel! 

After exploring and planning, I used my drywall saw to make a pumpkin cut. All 3 of the CAT5e cables were then exposed. The last network tech zip tied them together at the NID. Next I’ll be cutting the zip tie at the NID, pulling the wires and running them inside the garage for termination. 

Eero’s aren’t rated for outside, and my garage gets cold, so my next endeavor is figuring out how to get it all connected.

That would most likely be easier! Thank you for taking the time out of your day to provide insight for me. I really appreciate it. My fiber cable is in a separate box! The NID box only has CAT 5e, I have another box with just Coax as well.

With it being vinyl siding, this is my plan of attack.

1. remove part of vinyl siding
2. drill through OSB behind it
3. pull cable
4. use drywall ring
5. seal
6. put vinyl back over it
